title: Assign an IP address to an interface
summary: Manually set a static IP address for a network interface using ifconfig. This overrides any DHCP-assigned address.

steps.explain: Assign the desired IP address to the interface. This requires root privileges.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface, e.g., eth0.

placeholders.name: IP_ADDRESS
placeholders.description: The IP address to assign, e.g., 192.168.1.10.

alternatives.explain: Add an IP address in CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.1.10/24) to the interface. The '+' derives the broadcast address automatically.
alternatives.cmd: sudo ip address add <IP_ADDRESS>/<PREFIX_LEN> broadcast + dev <INTERFACE>

rollback.explain: To revert to DHCP, you typically need to restart the network service or use a network manager command, as ifconfig does not have a direct 'dhcp' flag. Alternatively, bring the interface down and up again if a DHCP client is running.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface.

rollback.explain: Bring the interface back up to trigger DHCP.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface.

warnings: Setting a static IP incorrectly can disconnect you from the network. Ensure the IP address is valid for your subnet and does not conflict with other devices.
